1	# Task 11: Polished car-paint object with clearcoat on a turntable
2	
3	Framework: Aura3D (`@aura3d/engine`, already installed in node_modules).
4	
5	Build a single-page browser app with the provided framework, served by vite, drawing into the existing canvas with id #app. Show a glossy, candy-red, car-paint finished object on a slowly rotating turntable in a dark showroom. Since no model files are provided, construct the object procedurally from smooth shapes, for example a rounded, streamlined capsule or bean body with a separate smooth cabin bump and four dark rubber wheel discs, or any other smooth body with clearly curved, large reflective panels. The paint must look like automotive paint: a deep coloured base layer with fine metallic flake sparkle, topped by a glossy clear coat that mirrors a studio environment (long soft-box strip reflections that bend over the curved panels). Add chrome trim, such as a thin ring or strip, and a dark glass or black cabin panel for contrast. The turntable is a circular platform with a subtle ring light or reflective floor on which the object is mirrored faintly. Use a dark background with two or three long strip lights above and to the sides, plus a faint cool rim light, so the reflections read as soft-box highlights. The platform rotates the object at about 20 degrees per second while the camera stays still at a low, slightly front-three-quarter angle with the whole object in frame. content.thinking:
I'll keep the camera static using a perspective setup with no orbit interaction. For reflections, I'm thinking the studio or materialLab environment presets likely include softbox strips, and rect area lights could also contribute visible specular highlights.

Since flake options aren't documented, I'll avoid speculative material fields like carPaint and stick with physical material using only well-documented properties such as metallic, roughness, and clearcoat to stay safe against typecheck failures.

For the sparkle effect, I'm considering adding hundreds of tiny instanced spheres scattered slightly above the ellipsoid body surface, with high metallic values and a small outward offset, to simulate flake glints under the clearcoat rather than relying on an unverified texture-based approach.

Checking that the pixel size works out at this distance and field of view, and giving the flakes warm gold/orange hues while making sure they don't cast shadows. Now sizing the car body as an ellipsoid stretched along the z-axis for length, with narrower width and lower height to match typical car proportions.

Working out wheel placement next, positioning cylindrical discs rotated to sit flush with the body, and checking whether the wheel edges clip through or stay outside the ellipsoid's curved surface at those x/z coordinates.

Then I'm adding chrome hub caps outboard of each wheel, raising the body's vertical position slightly, and building a glass cabin on top with a dark glossy material.

Torus geometry semantics feel too unpredictable for a clean belt ring, so I'm leaning toward a simpler alternative: using thin chrome capsule shapes as front and rear bumper trim instead.

For the side chrome strip, I realize a straight capsule would clip into the ellipsoid body at its ends, so I should instead place a chain of small chrome spheres along the belt-line ellipse to simulate a thin trim line, spacing them tightly enough (around 160 spheres, small diameter, spacing under the sphere diameter) so they read as a continuous bead of chrome.

I'm also planning a chrome ring at each hub, a front bumper bar made of the same instanced beads, and tiny chrome-ish spheres for headlights, while checking whether the chrome material function accepts a color parameter or should just use default pbr metallic/roughness settings for safety.

For glass I'll use a near-black physical material with low roughness and clearcoat for a glossy look, rubber tires get a dark high-roughness pbr, and the platform is a wide shallow cylinder. For the reflective floor effect I'm considering whether Aura supports a true reflective material or screen-space reflections, otherwise I'll fake it with a mirrored duplicate of the car underneath.

I'll skip the risky negative-scale mirror trick since it could break shading, and instead settle on a reflective glossy floor material paired with a ring light for the reflection effect, keeping things safe for headless rendering.

For lighting, I'll use studio environment IBL combined with softbox rect lights positioned above and to the sides, targeting the platform center.

To get real reflections of those softbox strips on the car paint, I realize I should use environments.capture to bake the scene into a cubemap, placing emissive strip meshes where the lights are so they actually show up as reflections. Since the capture is world-space, the car rotating will naturally produce sliding highlight reflections across the paint, which is the effect I want.

But self-capturing with the car in frame is risky, and I'm unsure if capture also provides diffuse IBL or just replaces the whole environment. Given the uncertainty, I think it's safer to fall back on the documented studio presets (like "studio" or "metalStudio") that already include built-in softbox lighting, rather than risk a black scene from a failed runtime capture.
